questions.q: What is a 'galaxy schema' as used in this capstone's model?
options: Multiple fact tables sharing dimension tables — still governed by the same star-schema modeling rules
A schema with no fact tables at all
A completely different modeling approach unrelated to star schemas
A schema that requires DirectQuery mode specifically
questions.explain: FactInternetSales and FactResellerSales both share dimensions like DimProduct and DimSalesTerritory — two fact tables, still following star-schema principles.

questions.q: How many of FactInternetSales's three date relationships (OrderDateKey, DueDateKey, ShipDateKey) can be active at once?
options: Only one — Power BI auto-activates OrderDateKey and leaves the other two inactive
All three are always active simultaneously
None of them are ever active by default
Exactly two are active, one is inactive
questions.explain: Only one relationship between two tables can be active at a time. Power BI activates OrderDateKey by default; DueDateKey and ShipDateKey stay inactive until activated via USERELATIONSHIP() in a measure.

questions.q: Why must DimDate be explicitly marked as the date table in this capstone, rather than relying on auto date/time?
options: DimDate relates to the fact tables via a whole-number surrogate key, not the date column itself — the exact scenario Lesson 47 said requires explicit marking
Auto date/time works perfectly fine here and marking is optional
DimDate has no date column at all
Marking a date table is only needed for DirectQuery models
questions.explain: This is the textbook surrogate-key scenario from Lesson 47 — a whole-number key relationship means auto date/time can't cover it, so DimDate must be explicitly marked.

questions.q: What cardinality should every relationship in this capstone's model show, with the dimension table on the '1' side?
options: One-to-many
Many-to-many
One-to-one
Zero-to-many
questions.explain: Standard star-schema relationships are one-to-many, with the dimension table on the 'one' side and the fact table on the 'many' side — if Power BI guesses differently, it needs to be corrected manually.

questions.q: What will Lesson 88's DAX measures need in order to use FactInternetSales's DueDateKey or ShipDateKey relationships?
options: USERELATIONSHIP(), to activate the inactive relationship for that specific calculation
A completely separate semantic model just for shipping dates
Nothing special — inactive relationships work exactly like active ones automatically
Deleting the OrderDateKey relationship entirely
questions.explain: Since only one date relationship is active by default, any measure needing to filter by DueDate or ShipDate specifically must use USERELATIONSHIP() to temporarily activate that relationship.
